title: Red Horse Airmen Learn Water Purification in Japan
description: Package about Airmen from the 554th Red Horse Squadron, stationed in Okinawa, Japan coming to Misawa Air Base to assist its’ Civil Engineer Squadron after the March 11th earthquake and tsunami. Includes sound bites from Tech. Sgt. Neil Stege and Airman 1st Class Daniel White. jpearthquake11, Operation Tomodachi
keywords: disaster relief, jpearthquake11, Operation Tomodachi, 554th Red Horse Squadron, water fuels maintenance, water purification

transcript.text: Airmen from the 554th Redhorse Squadron, station in Okinawa, Japan, came to Masawa Air Base
to assist its civil engineer squadron after the March 11th earthquake and tsunami.
While at Masawa, they took time to train some of its Airmen on the use of the reverse osmosis
water purification unit or ROPU.
We came up here first of all to help Masawa get back on their feet as far as to get the
fighter wing back up and going.
We got the units up here from Guam and we're up here making water just like we would down
in Okinawa at our training site.
These Airmen are exposed to unfamiliar aspects of their career field.
My job water field maintenance entails taking care of all the water and fuel lines on base.
This is the first time I've ever dealt with actual contingency ways of bringing water such
as the ROPU.
Otherwise I've just done basic supply of water on base.
This training consists of more than just the basics.
The Airmen are going to be in the water plant running the ROPU, making water and they need
to know the ins and outs, not just operations but they need to know maintenance and troubleshooting
and everything.
Job satisfaction and understanding why each specialty in the Air Force is important was
another thing these Airmen walked away with.
You feel like, you see, wow, this is actually really important.
You'll need water.
My job is legitimately important and I'm actually important to be here.
Petty Officer Sean Spratt, the Sawa Air Base, Japan.
